area: Backup restore drill feasibility (Solen.ch, Supabase project tocfnsmxmdxkrcmjzzdw)
summary: The nightly backup cron has never run once. The `db-backup` job exists in the local `.github/workflows/cron-jobs.yml`, but GitHub's default branch `main` was last pushed 2026-05-21 and its copy of that workflow has no `db-backup` job and no `'45 3 * * *'` schedule; the registered workflow is `disabled_inactivity` with 2,981 failures and 0 successes across 2,984 runs, and production `solen.ch/api/cron/db-backup` returns the HTML catch-all (route not deployed). I listed the live `db-backups` bucket read-only: it contains exactly one folder, `backups/2026-07-11/`, 24 files, 2.72 MB, written 16:39 UTC on the day the feature was built. So the real RPO today is 15 days 22 hours, not the "daily" the runbook implies, and it is growing. The 16%-of-tables figure checks out exactly (24 of 146 tables; 2,455 of 14,538 rows). More seriously, a restore into any fresh environment is structurally impossible right now for two independently verified reasons: (1) `profiles` and 10 other live tables have no `CREATE TABLE` anywhere in the 273 migration files, so the runbook's "provision schema from `supabase/migrations/`" step dies at file 2 of 273; (2) the backup set carries foreign keys into `auth.users`, which PostgREST cannot see (PGRST205) and which therefore can never be in the export. I proved (2) concretely: 3 of 47 `referrals.referrer_id` values point at auth users that have no `profiles` row, and live `auth.users` has 55 rows against 49 backed-up profiles. A restore is only possible onto a target that already carries the same `auth.users`, which means a `--with-data` Supabase branch, not a fresh project or a local Postgres.

findings.claim: BLOCKER 2, the decisive one: the backup set has foreign keys into `auth.users`, which the export mechanism structurally cannot capture. A fresh empty project cannot accept these rows.

Proven on the real artifact: 3 of 47 `referrals.referrer_id` values are absent from `profiles.json`; a read-only `GET /auth/v1/admin/users` count (no PII printed) shows `auth.users` = 55, backup profiles = 49, 6 auth users have no profile, 0 profiles lack an auth user, and all 3 orphan referrer_ids exist in `auth.users`. `supabase/migrations/014_new_schema.sql:61-64` confirms `profiles` is populated by an `AFTER INSERT ON auth.users` trigger, i.e. profiles is downstream of auth.

recommendation:
Run the drill in three ranked tiers, and fix the cron first because the drill validates a mechanism that is currently not running at all.

TIER 0, do this before anything else, ~10 minutes, $0, zero production write surface. Copy `backups/2026-07-11/` out of the bucket to durable storage. It is the only backup that exists and the first clean nightly run will prune it (`lib/backup/export.ts:143-150`, cutoff 14 days, folder is 16 days old). Then get the workflow onto GitHub: push main and re-enable the `disabled_inactivity` workflow, because `.github/workflows/cron-jobs.yml:15,183-194` exists only locally and the remote copy has no `db-backup` job.

TIER 1, the safest drill that proves something real, ~1 hour, $0, no database touched, and it has already found two defects. Write `scripts/restore-rehearsal.ts` modelled on `scripts/db-backup-kill-test.ts` (same env loading, same per-scenario PASS/FAIL report, same non-zero exit). It downloads a date folder read-only from the `db-backups` bucket and asserts, without any target database: every FK value resolves inside the backup set; the FK order in `_plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md:24` is a valid topological order and names columns that actually exist; every column present in the JSON exists in `_inventory/_db-columns.json`. Running this by hand today already returned 3 orphan `referrals.referrer_id` values and 4 columns named in the runbook that are not in the data. This closes half of H1 honestly: it names the exact blocker, which is what H1 explicitly permits. It does not produce an RTO number, so it does not close H2.

TIER 2, the only option that can produce a real restored database and a measured RTO, requires Pro. `supabase branches create <name> --with-data` is the single option where the restore can succeed, because `--with-data` clones production including `auth.users`, and without that clone 49 `profiles` rows and 3 `referrals` rows have no valid parent. Cost, from the pricing page fetched today, is $0.01344 per branch-hour, so a four-hour drill is about five cents, on top of Pro at $25/month if the project is still Free. Sequence: create the branch, point a copy of `.env.local` at the branch URL and keys, run the restore in FK order against the branch only, run `npm run smoke` with those overridden env vars (not the default, see below), time each step, then `supabase branches delete`. Two named risks: `--with-data` copies production personal data into a second database, which is an nFADP consideration the owner should acknowledge; and branch creation needs a Supabase access token plus a CLI that can reach api.supabase.com, which this sandbox cannot (TLS OSStatus -26276), though plain curl against the Management REST API works from here.

NOT recommended: a fresh second Supabase project (Free allows 2 active projects, so $0) and local Postgres via Docker both start with an empty `auth.users` and a migration replay that dies at `supabase/migrations/002_profiles.sql:1`. They cost the most work and prove the least. Local Postgres additionally needs a Docker Desktop install that does not exist on this machine.

Three things to fix regardless of tier, all one-liners or close. `_plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md:25` step 5 must say to override `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and the keys before running `npm run smoke`, because `scripts/api-smoke.ts:17-18` loads `.env.local` and would otherwise verify production and pass no matter what the restore did. `_plans/OPS_RUNBOOK.md:15` must stop claiming a fresh environment can be provisioned from files until the 11 missing CREATE TABLEs are backfilled. And `lib/backup/export.ts:26-51` should gain `promo_redemptions` and `salon_portfolio_images` at minimum.

LOUD PRODUCTION WARNINGS for whoever runs this. The Supabase CLI in this working directory is linked to production (`supabase/.temp/project-ref` = tocfnsmxmdxkrcmjzzdw): `supabase db push` and `supabase db dump` both default to `--linked`, so a bare command hits prod. Only one credential exists, the production service-role key, and it holds write plus delete on both the live database and the sole backup bucket. `scripts/db-backup-kill-test.ts` writes into the production Storage bucket, not a sandbox. If you relink the CLI to a different project for the drill, relink it back, because nothing warns you which project you are pointed at.
